directAnswer: Pope Honorius II was Lamberto Scannabecchi, cardinal bishop of Ostia and one of the negotiators of the Concordat of Worms, who reigned from 1124 to 1130. Elected amid pressure from the Frangipani family, he approved the Premonstratensians, saw the Knights Templar receive their rule, and contended with Roger II over southern Italy.

sections.h2: Lamberto of Fiagnano and the Concordat of Worms
paras: Lamberto was born of modest family at Fiagnano, in the territory of Casalfiumanese near Imola. He became a canon regular, archdeacon of Bologna, and later cardinal bishop of Ostia. Callixtus II sent him to Germany as legate, and he was one of the papal negotiators who concluded the Concordat of Worms in 1122.

When Callixtus II died in December 1124, a group of cardinals chose Cardinal Theobald Boccapecci, who took the name Celestine. Before he could be installed, Robert Frangipane and his armed supporters forced the acclamation of Lamberto instead. Theobald stepped aside to avoid bloodshed.

Uneasy about the irregular way he had been chosen, Lamberto resigned a few days later before the cardinals, who then elected him again. The episode revealed rivalries between Roman families, especially the Frangipani and the Pierleoni, that would split the Church at his death.

In 1126 Honorius approved the Order of Canons Regular founded by St. Norbert at Prémontré. Two years later, at the Council of Troyes, held in January 1129 by modern reckoning and attended by his legate, the Knights Templar received a formal rule; St. Bernard of Clairvaux was closely involved. This recognition made the Templars the first military religious order with a written rule approved by the Church.

sections.h2: Lothair III and Roger II of Sicily
paras: In Germany Honorius recognized the election of Lothair III in 1125, supporting him against the Hohenstaufen claimant Conrad. In southern Italy he tried to stop Roger II of Sicily from taking over the duchy of Apulia, even preaching a campaign against him, but in 1128 he was forced to invest Roger as duke.
Honorius died in Rome on February 13, 1130. His death set off the schism between Innocent II and Anacletus II.

keyFacts: Personal name: Lamberto Scannabecchi, cardinal bishop of Ostia
Papal negotiator of the Concordat of Worms (1122)
The Knights Templar received their rule at the Council of Troyes in the late 1120s
Invested Roger II as duke of Apulia (1128)

faqs.question: Why did Honorius II resign right after his election?
faqs.answer: He had been forced into office by the Frangipani over a candidate the cardinals had already chosen. To resolve doubts, he resigned before the cardinals, who promptly elected him again.

faqs.question: Did Honorius II approve the Knights Templar?
faqs.answer: The Templars received their rule at the Council of Troyes during his pontificate, with his legate present and St. Bernard of Clairvaux closely involved.

faqs.question: Which religious order founded by St. Norbert did Honorius II approve?
faqs.answer: In 1126 he approved the Premonstratensian canons, also called Norbertines, founded at Prémontré.
